summary: Turning a CAD model into a machining program requires both process knowledge and geometric precision. Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task.
takeaways: With Qwen3.8-27B, MillBill outperforms frontier-model approaches that construct their own geometry and toolpath workflows on the evaluated machining tasks.
Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task.
We introduce MillBill, an agent that separates machining decisions from their geometric execution and verification.
